subject: environmental-science
title: Maximum Sustainable Yield
welcome_lead: How much fish can we take forever — and where does that magic number come?
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on MSY, logistic growth and stock recruitment.
final_note: MSY is theoretically elegant — but ignoring environmental variability has emptied many seas.

concepts.def: Largest catch that can be sustained indefinitely; at N = K/2 under logistic growth.
Annual catch limit set by managers; allocated as quotas.
Addition of young fish to the exploitable population.
Relationship between spawning biomass and recruitment (Beverton-Holt, Ricker).
Setting catch limits below MSY to allow for uncertainty (FAO 1995).

walkthroughs.body_html: Under logistic growth dN/dt = rN(1−N/K), maximum surplus production occurs at N = K/2.
Beverton-Holt asymptotes to a maximum; Ricker curves rise then fall, capturing density-dependent egg cannibalism.
Cod off Newfoundland collapsed in 1992 despite TAC management — environmental shifts shifted recruitment.
